title: RichTextLabel visible_ratio behaviour when text changes is inconsistent with Label
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.4, 4.6.3, 4.7.beta3
- Not reproducible in: Tested 4.0 and 4.3, `Label`'s behaviour was even more buggy before 4.4 so let's just assume 4.4 as a baseline for the current behaviour.

### System information

Godot v4.7.beta3 - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.16.1047) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Changing the text of a `Label` or `RichTextLabel` has different, inconsistent behaviour on the values ot `visible_ratio` and `visible_characters`, if they are set to non-default values:

1. For `Label`, `visible_ratio` is used as the source of truth. It stays the same, while `visible_characters` is recalculated to match the new text length. (The exception to this is if `visible_characters` is set to the length of the string; then the behaviour is broken as reported in #119837.)
2. For `RichTextLabel`, `visible_characters` is used as the source of truth. The new text is truncated to match `visible_characters`. (Note that `visible_ratio` should therefore update to match the new length, but it doesn't, again a case of #119837.)

(This is an extension of my previous bug report #119837 which relates to the behaviour of `visible_ratio` and `visible_characters` in `Label` and `RichTextLabel`. I'm reporting a separate bug because there's an independent question of whether `RichTextLabel` should be brought in line to match `Label`'s behaviour.)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a `Label` or `RichTextLabel` with `text = "Short text"` (len=10).
2. Set `visible_characters = 6`, the exact length of the text. (This sets `visible_ratio` to 0.6.)
3. Set `text` to a new, longer string, `"Very long text, so so long"` (len=26).

For `Label`, the new text is truncated to 60% of its length (preserving the `visible_ratio`) and `visible_characters` is recomputed to 15.

For `RichTextLabel`, the new text is truncated to 6 characters (preserving the `visible_characters`). `visible_ratio` stays at 0.6, which is #119837.

Three choices here:

A. Keep inconsistent (least breaking change). Fix #119837 by making `RichTextLabel` recalculate `visible_ratio` to match reality.
B. Make `RichTextlabel` consistent with `Label`. The text is truncated to 60% of its length, and `visible_characters` is recomputed.
C. Make `Label` consistent with `RichTextLabel`. The text is truncated to 6 characters, and `visible_ratio` is recomputed.

My preference is for B or C (for consistency). Since `RichTextLabel`'s behaviour is more broken than `Label`, slight preference for B (changing `RichTextLabel`). Note that I can easily do any of these in my pull request for #119837.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[visible_ratio_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28339870/visible_ratio_test.zip)

(This is my MRP for #119837 but it can also be used to demonstrate this by changing the type of the `Label` to `RichTextLabel` and observing the differences.)
